cosy-lesson.title: "Study hard what interests you the most in the most undisciplined, irreverent and original manner possible.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Unorthodox – contrary to what is usual, traditional, or accepted within academic institutions.

p.em: Example: His unorthodox method of teaching physics involved playing bongo drums in class.

cosy-blockquote.p: Subversive – seeking to disrupt, challenge, or subvert an established system, custom, or authority.

p.em: Example: Studying what you love instead of what is graded can feel like a highly subversive act.

cosy-blockquote.p: Innovative – featuring new methods; advanced, fresh, and highly creative in design.

p.em: Example: Feynman diagrams were incredibly innovative, completely changing how physicists view particles.

cosy-blockquote.p: Predilection – a strong preference, special liking, or natural bias in favor of a specific topic.

p.em: Example: She had a strong predilection for biology, spending hours analyzing forest ecosystems.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prescribed – recommended, laid down as a rule, or officially required by a course syllabus.

p.em: Example: He quickly finished the prescribed textbook and started reading advanced research papers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insubordination – refusal to obey strict, rigid orders or bow down to established academic authority.

p.em: Example: His constant questions were seen as a sign of insubordination by the traditional department head.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pioneer – a person who is among the first to explore, study, or develop a new area of knowledge.

p.em: Example: As a scientific pioneer, Feynman refused to let old dogmas limit his imagination.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dogma – a principle or set of rules laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true.

p.em: Example: Challenging academic dogma is essential if you want to discover genuine scientific breakthroughs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nonconformist – a person whose behavior, style, or views do not conform to prevailing social ideas.

p.em: Example: A nonconformist mind is highly valuable in a world that rewards quiet, quiet obedience.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vigor – intense physical or mental strength, energy, and robust enthusiasm for an activity.

p.em: Example: She attacked the difficult mathematical equations with admirable, youthful vigor.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the danger of relying purely on a prescribed educational syllabus without any independent research?
★ Have you ever had a strong predilection for a topic that was not in your school syllabus?

Why do major scientific breakthroughs require an unorthodox, playful approach?
★ What is the most unorthodox habit or custom you practice in your daily work?

Why are self-taught learners often accused of insubordination by traditional authorities?
★ Have you ever rebelled against a rigid academic or corporate dogma?

How does a nonconformist style of thought help us discover highly innovative ideas?
★ Do you consider your own style of working to be highly innovative or traditional?

How can we pursue our creative vigor while respecting the strict rigor of our profession?
★ What creative project are you currently pursuing with your greatest energy and vigor?

Why did Feynman believe that being a scientific pioneer requires a healthy irreverence for authority?
★ Who is an intellectual pioneer you deeply admire, and what have they taught you?

How can a student stay motivated when studying a subject that is completely subversive to social expectations?
★ Have you ever felt that your hobbies or passions were a bit subversive to your community?

Why does a standardized school syllabus often ignore a child's natural predilection for play?
★ If you had complete autonomy as a child, which unorthodox topic would you have explored?

How does challenging established academic dogma protect us from intellectual complacency?
★ Do you find it easy to spot dogmas in your professional field or career?

What does it mean to be a true pioneer in your personal career or study over the next decade?
★ If you could master one complex skill with absolute vigor, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is a nonconformist, unorthodox study method most helpful? Rank them: - 🎸 Creative Passion Developing an original artistic style by completely ignoring prescribed rules, conventions, and textbook dogmas. - 🔬 Scientific Discovery Pioneering a new branch of physics by playing bongo drums and sketching irrelevant, unorthodox particle diagrams. - 💻 Innovative Tech Writing highly subversive software that challenges corporate authority and established tech conventions. - 📈 Financial Speculation Having a strong predilection for high-risk, unorthodox assets while ignoring traditional prescribed investments.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, corporate recruiting will fully ban standard diplomas, hiring only candidates with highly unorthodox self-taught portfolios. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you encourage your children to skip university if they had a clear, innovative passion?

Smart algorithms will eventually make all prescribed scientific education obsolete, allowing humans to focus purely on creative pioneering. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you trust an AI doctor whose diagnosing logic was completely unorthodox?

Future societies will prioritize extreme cognitive autonomy, viewing academic dogma as a sign of mental weakness. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you hope future generations will possess more cognitive freedom than today's children?

Virtual reality study circles will allow students to practice completely subversive and creative research without any corporate censorship. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you join a virtual group that openly challenges established political dogmas?

As artificial intelligence automates all analytical fields, human workers will be valued purely for their nonconformist creative vigor. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is one complex skill you hope to master with your greatest vigor?

Future schools will completely eliminate the prescribed syllabus, evaluating students purely on their natural predilection. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you send your children to a school that has no prescribed grading system?

In the coming decades, choosing not to conform to corporate customs will be seen as a highly valuable innovative trait. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe that staying fully nonconformist is the ultimate key to professional happiness?

Global digital networks will make it incredibly simple to synthesize multiple unorthodox sciences into one breakthrough. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees safety at the cost of your freedom?

In tomorrow's world, social status will be determined by how subversive and original your thoughts are rather than your wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope creative vigor will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A future world fully governed by smart logic will leave no space left for the quiet mystery of individual insubordination. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to exercise greater personal autonomy right now?

ul.li: Incorrect: I want to study more hard → Correct: I want to study harder ((Comparative form of 'hard' is 'harder'))
Incorrect: I am interest in Feynman → Correct: I am interested in Feynman ((Use passive participle adjective 'interested' instead of noun))
Incorrect: She learn English fastly → Correct: She learns English quickly ((Third-person singular 's', adverb 'quickly'))
